colour.reasoning: The undertone evidence reads warm: golden-tan skin with warm brown shadows sits close to the camel overshirt without going sallow, the olive tee does not grey it, and the silver watch reads as a contrast rather than a match. I discounted this slightly because the observer noted a warm cream cast from the backdrop. Clarity reads muted rather than clear, since the dusty camel and olive sit well and the lips are a muted warm brown-rose. Depth comes from the medium skin and the very deep near-black hair with dark brown eyes, which together with the medium contrast point to a deep autumn rather than a soft or bright season.

skin.undertone_evidence: Skin reads golden-tan with warm brown shadows at the neck and jaw; it sits close in value and warmth to the camel overshirt without looking sallow, and the olive tee does not turn it grey. The silver watch is a cool contrast point rather than a match. Lips are muted warm brown-rose. The warm cream backdrop may be adding some warmth.

Brushed gold, brass or bronze on a brown leather strap will look like it belongs to your skin, and it echoes the brown bead bracelet you already wear.

decisions.must_axis_why: Your skin turns rich next to camel and olive and stays clear of grey, so warmth is what makes colour work on you. A cool icy shade loses that glow at once, so whatever you buy outside this fan, keep it warm.
decisions.flexible_axis_why: Your very deep hair, strong brows and full beard give you enough definition to carry a slightly crisper shade without it overpowering you, as your white sneakers show. You can go a touch cleaner than dusty, as long as it stays warm and deep.

avoid.name: Icy grey
avoid.why: It pulls the warmth out of your skin and leaves the jaw and under-eye area looking grey and tired.

avoid.name: Pastel lilac
avoid.why: Cool and light at once, it fights your golden undertone and makes your deep hair and beard look heavy by comparison.

avoid.name: Electric cobalt
avoid.why: Too bright and too cool for your muted warmth; it takes the attention away from your face.

decisions.changing_room_test: Take the shirt to a window and hold it flat under your chin. If the skin along your beard line and under your eyes turns grey or ashy, put it back; if your skin looks golden and your brows and beard look sharper, it is yours.
decisions.archetype_why: You already dress in a few calm, tonal pieces with no logos and no fuss, which is exactly the clean and minimal look you want. Your tall frame and broader shoulders carry simple, well-cut layers without needing decoration.
decisions.style_words_why: Easy is what you wear now: an open overshirt with rolled sleeves over a relaxed tee. Polished is the step up your formal work days ask for, with sharper collars and structured trousers in the same calm colours. Warm ties it together: camel, olive and earth tones are what make your skin glow.

face.shape: Oval: balanced length and width, with visible cheekbones and a defined jaw under your beard. Most collar and neckline shapes suit you, so you can choose them for the occasion.

necklines.what: An open collar with the top one or two buttons undone, forming a soft V
necklines.why: Your neck is average length and your beard already fills the jaw. A V opens the space between beard and chest, which lengthens the neck and keeps the look clean rather than crowded.
necklines.evidence: Face notes: 'Average neck length, partly hidden by open collar'; 'Full, close-trimmed dark beard'.

necklines.what: A clean crew neck that sits close at the base of the neck, never stretched or wide
necklines.why: The crew neck already works on you as a base layer. A firm, close neckline keeps a crisp line under your beard edge and fits the clean, minimal look you want.
necklines.evidence: Outfit notes: olive crew-neck T-shirt worn under the open overshirt; facial_hair notes 'clean cheek line and neat edges'.

necklines.what: A shallow V-neck knit or polo-style knit collar for dates and evenings
necklines.why: It keeps the elongating V in a softer, dressier fabric than a T-shirt. It also suits your oval face without adding bulk at the throat.
necklines.evidence: Face shape 'oval'; 'Average neck length'; occasions include 'dates and evenings'.

collars.what: A semi-spread or spread collar with medium-length points for formal work shirts
collars.why: Medium points match the scale of your face and your strong, straight brows. A spread frames the beard neatly when you wear a tie or button the shirt to the top.
collars.evidence: Face notes: 'Strong, dark, fairly straight brows'; 'Defined jawline under a full trimmed beard'; occasions include 'formal work'.

collars.what: A band (mandarin) collar: a bandhgala, a Nehru jacket over a kurta, or a band-collar linen shirt
collars.why: A band collar is very clean and minimal, and it sits below your beard line without competing with it. It also gives you a formal option that breathes better than a full suit in heat.
collars.evidence: Heritage read 'South Asian'; vibe 'clean and minimal'; climate 'hot and humid'; 'Average neck length'.

collars.what: A camp (Cuban) collar shirt in linen or cotton for evenings
collars.why: It lies flat and open, so it gives you the V without effort. It is also one of the coolest collar styles for humid nights.
collars.evidence: Climate 'hot and humid'; occasions 'dates and evenings'; neck 'partly hidden by open collar'.

glasses.what: If you add frames or sunglasses, choose medium-weight rectangular or soft-square shapes, such as a classic wayfarer, in dark tortoiseshell or deep brown
glasses.why: An oval face carries most shapes. Slightly squared lines echo your straight brows and defined jaw, and a medium frame weight holds its own against your dark hair and beard without overpowering your face.
glasses.evidence: Face notes: glasses false; 'Strong, dark, fairly straight brows'; hair 'near-black'; full dark beard.

hair.what: Keep the short tapered sides with length and volume on top, styled up and back
hair.why: Height on top gives your oval face a strong vertical line. It also balances the width your full beard adds lower down, and the tight sides keep everything neat for work.
hair.evidence: Hair notes: 'Short tapered sides, longer top styled up and back into a voluminous quiff with visible wave; neat, defined hairline'.

earrings_or_scale.what: A watch case of about 39 to 42 mm with a slim profile, and collar points of medium length
earrings_or_scale.why: You are tall with an average frame, so mid-size details look proportionate. A slim case also slides under a shirt cuff for formal work.
earrings_or_scale.evidence: Build: frame 'average', height_impression 'tall'; accessories note 'Silver-tone analogue wristwatch with metal bracelet'.

body.summary: Tall and average in frame, with shoulders wider than hips and a balanced torso and legs: a naturally strong, athletic top half that needs only light balancing below.

silhouettes.what: Open layers over a fitted base: an overshirt, an unstructured blazer or a Nehru jacket worn over a slim tee or shirt
silhouettes.why: The open front draws a vertical line down your body, which uses your height and your strong shoulders well. It is already your strongest look.
silhouettes.evidence: Outfit: camel overshirt 'worn open' over olive crew-neck tee; build 'tall', shoulders vs hips 'wider'.

silhouettes.what: Soft-shouldered or unstructured blazers and jackets, with no padding
silhouettes.why: Your shoulders already carry width, so padding would make you top-heavy. Soft construction also keeps you cooler in humid weather.

silhouettes.what: Straight or gently tapered trousers with a little room through the thigh, rather than very skinny legs
silhouettes.why: A leg with some substance balances your wider shoulders, so the line from shoulder to shoe reads even and long.

rise_and_lengths.what: Mid-rise trousers that sit at or just below the navel, with a belt for formal work
rise_and_lengths.why: With a balanced torso and legs, a mid rise keeps your proportions even and holds a tucked shirt neatly through a working day.

rise_and_lengths.what: Formal trousers: full length with a slight break or none, no cuff, hem just touching the shoe
rise_and_lengths.why: A clean, uninterrupted line suits your height and the minimal look you want. Keep the cuffed, above-ankle hem for casual denim.
rise_and_lengths.evidence: Outfit: jeans 'cuffed hems… ending just above the ankle when cuffed'; vibe 'clean and minimal'.

rise_and_lengths.what: Untucked shirts and overshirts ending at the upper hip, around mid-fly; jacket hems covering the seat
rise_and_lengths.why: This keeps your leg line long and your shoulders balanced. The overshirt length you already wear is right.
rise_and_lengths.evidence: Outfit: overshirt 'hem ends at upper hip'; tee 'untucked'.

rise_and_lengths.what: Shirt sleeves ending at the wrist bone, with about 1 cm of cuff showing past a jacket sleeve
rise_and_lengths.why: On a tall frame, short sleeves expose the wrist and look outgrown. Correct sleeve length makes formal outfits look tailored.
rise_and_lengths.evidence: Build: height_impression 'tall'; outfit: overshirt 'sleeves rolled to forearm'.

print_scale.what: Small to medium, low-contrast prints and textures: fine checks, tonal stripes, waffle or slub weaves, small geometric camp-shirt prints
print_scale.why: Your colouring is muted and medium in contrast, so soft, tonal pattern sits better than bold, high-contrast prints. Texture adds interest while keeping the look minimal.
print_scale.evidence: Colour analysis: contrast medium, clarity muted; outfit tee 'possibly fine waffle or textured knit'.

accessory_scale.what: Mid-size, refined accessories: a slim watch, one bracelet at a time, belts about 3 to 3.5 cm wide
accessory_scale.why: These suit your average frame and height and keep the clean, minimal feel. One statement piece per wrist is enough.
accessory_scale.evidence: Accessories: 'Silver-tone analogue wristwatch with metal bracelet' and 'Brown wooden or stone bead bracelet'; frame 'average'.

fabric_weight.what: Light to mid-weight, breathable fabrics: linen, cotton-linen, seersucker, chambray, tropical wool for formal trousers, and light cotton twill for overshirts
fabric_weight.why: In humid heat, breathable fabrics keep you sharp all day. Your average frame doesn't need heavy fabric to give shape, and a soft drape suits the unstructured lines that work for you.
fabric_weight.evidence: Climate 'hot and humid'; outfit overshirt 'cotton twill or brushed cotton'; jeans 'raw or rinse denim'; frame 'average'.

fit_fixes.what: For work and dates, choose straight-leg trousers, or have a tailor ease the taper slightly from knee to hem
fit_fixes.why: A slightly fuller lower leg balances your shoulders and looks more polished with formal shoes.

fit_fixes.what: Have shirts and blazers fitted through the chest and shoulders first, then take in the waist
fit_fixes.why: Your shoulders are your widest point. Fit them first, then remove excess at the waist so there is no billowing.

fit_fixes.what: Make sure T-shirts end at mid-fly when untucked, with sleeves hitting mid-bicep
fit_fixes.why: This keeps the base layer clean under an open layer and stops it lengthening your torso beyond your balanced proportions.
fit_fixes.evidence: Outfit: crew-neck tee 'untucked', fit 'regular'; build torso_vs_legs 'balanced'.

grooming.what: Keep the full, close-trimmed beard with clean cheek lines and neat edges. Tidy the neckline about two fingers above the Adam's apple every few days.
grooming.why: It defines your jaw and adds structure to your oval face. In heat, a crisp neckline keeps it looking deliberate rather than overgrown.

grooming.what: Keep the tapered sides and voluminous top. Use a matte, humidity-resistant clay or paste, and refresh the taper every 3 to 4 weeks.
grooming.why: The height flatters your face and suits work and evenings alike. A matte hold keeps your natural wave in shape in humid air without looking greasy.

grooming.what: Keep the watch size, but swap the metal bracelet for a brown leather or suede strap on formal days and dates.
grooming.why: A warm brown strap ties the watch into your camel, olive and brown palette and feels dressier, while the case stays exactly as it is.

grooming.what: Keep the brown bead bracelet for casual and evening looks, worn on the wrist opposite your watch.
grooming.why: Its warm, natural brown sits well with your golden-tan skin and adds a relaxed touch without clutter. Leave it off for the most formal work days.

grooming.what: Keep the brows natural and full, removing only stray hairs between them. Use a light, oil-free SPF moisturiser daily.
grooming.why: Your strong, straight brows anchor your face. In humid heat, a light, matte layer keeps skin even and shine-free for photos and evenings.

free.headline: Deep autumn, where camel and olive make your skin glow
working_lines: Camel overshirt and olive tee sit in your palette, keeping skin warm and healthy near your face.
Your close beard line and tall quiff define your jaw and lengthen your oval face.
Dark tapered jeans and white sneakers balance your broad shoulders and keep the base minimal.
free.change_line: Swap the silver metal-bracelet watch for a gold-tone dial on cognac leather. It's the one cool note in your warm look.
free.palette_caption: Wear these colours near your face and keep everything outside them warm.

colour.intro: You are a deep autumn: warm skin, very dark hair and beard, medium contrast and a muted tone. Undertone is the axis you cannot bend. Your skin turns rich next to camel and olive and goes flat next to cool, icy shades. Clarity is where you have room. Your dark hair, strong brows and full beard give you enough definition for a slightly cleaner shade, as your white sneakers show. So go a touch crisper than dusty if you like, but keep every colour warm and deep.
colour.how_to_combine: Put your strongest colours at your face: olive, rust, teal and oxblood. Build the rest of the outfit on espresso, ivory, ink indigo, stone and cognac, so the colour has a calm base. Petrol ink, aubergine and sage khaki are your extras. Keep them deep and warm, and use them away from the face first.

line.face_intro: Your face is oval, with visible cheekbones and a defined jaw under the beard. Your straight brows and full beard lead. That means most necklines work, so pick by occasion. An open V or a camp collar suits you best. Keep a medium collar point, and choose medium-weight rectangular or soft-square frames in dark tortoiseshell if you add glasses.
line.body_intro: You are tall with an average frame, shoulders wider than your hips, and balanced torso and legs. Your top half is already strong, so the work happens below and in the construction. Soft, unpadded shoulders keep you from looking top-heavy. Straight legs with some thigh room even out the line from shoulder to shoe. Open layers use your height, and sleeves that reach the wrist bone make everything look tailored.

style.what_you_wear: Your photo outfit is a camel overshirt worn open, an olive tee, dark slim jeans with a cuff and white sneakers. It works. The camel and olive are tonal, warm and sit well near your face. The open layer draws a vertical line down your body, and the dark tapered jeans balance your shoulders. Only the silver watch is off.
style.what_it_says: This reads as someone who does not need to try. Nothing has a logo or shouts. Calm, tonal pieces say you are relaxed and in control, and the clean fit says you pay attention. That suits the clean minimal look you asked for, and your tall frame carries it without any decoration.
style.the_words: Your three words are easy, polished and warm. Easy is what you wear now. Polished is the step up for formal work: sharper collars and structured trousers in the same calm colours. Warm is the colour rule. Before you buy anything, ask if it is easy, polished and warm. If it misses two of the three, leave it.

report.outfits_intro: These six outfits are built for the four settings you gave us: hybrid days, hot and humid weather, formal work, and dates and evenings. Your photo outfit is the first one, kept almost whole. The rest follow the same calm logic, and each one can be refined.
report.buy_intro: Buy in the order shown. The gold-tone watch is first because it fixes the one off note and unlocks four outfits. Use the search terms as written; they are tuned to the colour and cut. Each item lists the outfits it opens up, so you can see what it adds before you pay.
report.grooming_intro: Your grooming already does a lot of work. The beard and the quiff are right, so the changes are small: keep them tidy, use a matte hold that survives humidity, and swap the watch strap. Keep skin care light and oil-free for the heat.
report.closing: Remember one thing: keep everything warm and deep, and the rest follows. This week, swap your silver bracelet watch for a gold-tone dial on a cognac leather strap. Wear it on Tuesday with your camel overshirt. It is the smallest change that makes the biggest difference.
